rationales.net_cash: Net cash is computed by code as cash and cash equivalents plus short- and long-term marketable investments less total debt, at 2026-09-03: cash $38.364B (F-455b2cbdf8) + marketable investments $35.089B (S-0f9cbd5118 = short-term AvailableForSaleSecuritiesDebtSecuritiesCurrent $5.070B F-e8f2f41b64 + long-term AvailableForSaleSecuritiesDebtSecuritiesNoncurrent $30.019B F-5368223b24, as mapped by gen-mapping) - total debt $5.179B (S-0a86662e54 = current debt $0.491B + long-term debt including finance leases $4.688B; agrees with DebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations F-07b727110b) = $68.274B. The investments are available-for-sale investment-grade fixed-income securities that management counts in cash and marketable investments of $73.45B, so both the short- and the long-term portions belong in net cash. Non-marketable equity investments (about $1.30B in other noncurrent assets) are excluded as illiquid. A code dry run in memory on the round-2 mapping (it wrote no files and did not run eu.py compute) confirmed investments of $35.089B and net cash of $68.274B; the code output is authoritative. Refundable customer deposits: the $12.895B of noncurrent customer contract liabilities (F-3212bef088; periodic.txt balance sheet 'Noncurrent customer contract liabilities | 12,895', $142M a year earlier) are excluded from debt. They are treated as an operating contract liability, so net cash is not reduced by them. Reasons: (i) the 10-K classifies them as contract liabilities, not debt, they carry no stated interest, and the company states that 'Customer deposits do not represent significant financing components because the payments are primarily intended to secure future production capacity and ensure supply availability rather than provide financing to us' (periodic.txt ~line 2344). (ii) They are conditional. A deposit is returned only if the customer meets its minimum purchase commitments, and otherwise Micron 'may retain all or a portion of the deposit' (~line 1763), so they are not an unconditional borrowing. Acknowledged counter-argument: the $12.747B inflow came through financing cash flow ('Proceeds from customer contract liability deposits', cash flow statement ~line 2228), so it sits inside reported cash and hence inside net cash. In addition, 'Nearly all of the deposits are scheduled to be repaid between 2029 and 2031' (~lines 1763, 2961). That falls in DCF years 3-5, and the FCF path does not include the repayment. My normalization scenario has revenue falling in years 3-4, so I do not assume the deposits roll over into new ones. This makes the exclusion a judgment that favours the stock. Sensitivity, as analyst arithmetic and not code output: treating the full balance as debt-like would cut net cash to about $55.4B and reduce both the DCF and the EV/Sales per-share legs by about $11.3 ($12.895B / 1,145M diluted shares). Blended value would fall by about $11, roughly 1%. If instead the 2029-2031 repayment is discounted at the 10.5% WACC, the reduction is about $8 per share. The note should carry this as a valuation caveat.
rationales.wacc: 10.5%. This is analyst judgment: the snapshot has no beta, risk-free rate or credit spread. Micron is a commodity-memory manufacturer whose revenue and margins swing hard across the cycle. FY2025 FCF margin was about 4.5% and FY2026 about 44.3% (see fcf_margin). That cyclicality calls for an equity risk premium above the semiconductor average. Capital structure: interest-bearing debt is $5.179B (S-0a86662e54: current debt $0.491B plus long-term debt including finance leases $4.688B). Micron also holds $12.895B of non-interest-bearing refundable customer deposits (noncurrent customer contract liabilities, F-3212bef088), mostly scheduled to be repaid between 2029 and 2031. These are treated as operating contract liabilities rather than financing; see the net_cash rationale for the reasons and an approximately $11-per-share sensitivity. Even if they are counted, total debt-like claims of about $18.1B are far below cash plus short- and long-term marketable investments of $73.453B ($38.364B cash F-455b2cbdf8 + $35.089B investments S-0f9cbd5118). Net cash is therefore $68.274B, or about $55.4B with the deposits deducted, and the debt weight in WACC is negligible, so WACC is effectively the cost of equity. 10.5% sits inside the gate band [6%, 16%] and above the roughly 9-10% one would use for a less cyclical large-cap semiconductor company. No precise market-implied input was available to calibrate it. Unchanged from round 1.
rationales.terminal_growth: 3.0%: long-run nominal growth for a memory supplier whose bit demand is tied to data-center/AI and device content growth [Q-7, Q-8]. It is held at about nominal GDP, not above it, because memory pricing mean-reverts and the business is capital-intensive. The terminal value starts from a year-5 revenue level that has already been normalized below peak (see revenue_growth) and a mid-cycle FCF margin of 30%. It is within the gate band [0, 4%]. Unchanged from round 1.
rationales.revenue_growth: Year 1 (NTM) revenue is set by code from assumptions.json: about $269.5B, anchored on the FQ1-27 revenue guidance of $61.5B [Q-1]. Years 2-5 are +5%, -10%, -15%, -5%. This is analyst judgment for a cycle peak followed by normalization. Year 2 is still positive because demand exceeds industry supply [Q-7, Q-8], management expects an even stronger FY2027 [Q-6], and strategic customer agreements with price bands are in place [Q-9, Q-12]. Years 3-5 assume supply catches up and pricing falls toward the price-band floors, since memory has always mean-reverted after supply-constrained peaks. Even after the decline, year-5 revenue (about $206B) stays well above FY2026's $133.2B because of the higher price floors [Q-9]. Downside from export restrictions [Q-11] is not modeled separately. Unchanged from round 1.
rationales.fcf_margin: Years 1-5: 50%, 50%, 42%, 35%, 30%. Year 1 is lowered from 55% in round 1 to 50%. Historical grounding: FCF = CFO (mapped NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities) minus capex (PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment), divided by revenue, all from `eu.py history`. FY2025: CFO $17.525B less capex $15.857B on revenue $37.378B = 4.5%. FY2026: CFO $89.675B less capex $30.712B on revenue $133.188B = 44.3%. FY2026 by quarter: Q1 22.1% (F-e8854ed703, F-f322f0ab0e, F-b11cd8f3c2); Q2 23.1%; Q3 42.4% (D-0a072dc8dc, D-dc2ab297af, F-03e050e3a0); Q4 60.6% (D-21b02a031c, D-17b54bd7f0, D-e90aac72b9), a 14-week quarter [Q-10]. FY2026Q4 CFO was flattered by noncurrent income taxes payable from Pillar Two (other noncurrent liabilities +$9.633B for FY2026 in the cash flow statement). The $12.747B of customer deposits came through financing, not CFO, so they do not inflate these margins. Capex guidance, quoted verbatim from the 10-K (periodic.txt ~line 1771): 'We estimate capital expenditures for property, plant, and equipment, net of proceeds from government incentives, to be approximately $11.5 billion in the first quarter of 2027, approximately $25 billion in the first six months of 2027, and higher in the second half of 2027.' That implies FY2027 net capex above $50B, against $27.4B net in FY2026 ($30.712B gross less $3.316B government incentives). Year-1 reconciliation, which is analyst arithmetic and not code output, using code NTM figures where they exist: NTM net income $188.7B (code forecast from assumptions.json; it excludes interest income, which is correctly left out because the investments are already in net cash), plus D&A of about $12B (FY2026 $9.503B, rising with PP&E, which grew from $46.6B to $63.3B), plus stock-based compensation of about $1.5B (FY2026 $1.333B), less net capex of about $55B (the guided $25B first half plus a higher second half of about $30B), less working-capital absorption of about $12B. The working-capital figure assumes receivables stay at about 0.67x quarterly revenue (FY2026 year-end receivables $36.197B against Q4 revenue $54.229B). On the modeled FY2027Q4 revenue of about $71.8B, receivables then rise by about $11.8B, before small inventory and payables effects. Result: about $135B of FCF, or about 50% of NTM revenue of $269.5B. Range: capex at the $50B floor with $8B of working capital gives about 53.5%. Capex of $60B with $15B of working capital gives about 47%. 55% would require capex at the floor and almost no working-capital build, so it was the top of the range, and year 1 is set at the 50% centre. A recurring Pillar Two tax deferral is possible upside but is not assumed. Year 2 stays at 50%. The same arithmetic on about $283B of revenue (+5%), with higher capex of about $60B and only a small working-capital build, gives about 53%. Holding 50% allows for early price softening. Margins then fall with pricing in years 3-5. The 30% terminal margin is below the two-year pooled FY2025-FY2026 FCF margin of 35.5% ($60.6B FCF on $170.6B revenue). It is a mid-cycle figure: above the FY2025 trough because price-band floors keep gross margins above past peaks [Q-9], and below the peak because capex intensity rises in relative terms in a downturn. In the dry run the terminal share of EV is about 56%, under the 80% watch level; code is authoritative.
rationales.peers: INTC, AMAT, LRCX, KLAC. Micron is a capital-intensive, fab-owning memory manufacturer, and the covered/comps universe has no other memory maker. INTC is the only other integrated device manufacturer with owned fabs and heavy capex. AMAT, LRCX and KLAC are wafer-fab-equipment suppliers whose revenue is driven by the same memory/foundry capex cycle (LRCX in particular is memory-heavy), so their multiples carry similar cycle risk. Excluded: fabless/IP, AI-accelerator and connectivity names (NVDA, AMD, AVGO, MRVL, ALAB, CRDO, MPWR), because their asset-light models and growth profiles earn structurally higher, less cyclical multiples. EDA software (SNPS, CDNS) is excluded because it has recurring software economics. Peer TTM periods end between 2026-06-27 and 2026-07-26 (CY2026Q2), against Micron's 2026-09-03; all are within the 120-day alignment gate. Caveat: none of these peers is a memory maker, so the median EV/Sales (about 15.1x at cutoff closes) has no adjustment for memory's lower through-cycle margins. Unchanged from round 1.
rationales.dcf_weight: 0.75 DCF / 0.25 peer EV/Sales. The DCF explicitly models the guided next-four-quarter ramp and a cycle normalization. The EV/Sales cross-check is weak for Micron in two opposing ways. (1) Micron's TTM revenue ($133.2B) understates its current run-rate, since FY2026Q4 alone was $54.2B; this biases relative value down. (2) The peers are not memory makers, and their multiples reflect less cyclical margin structures; this biases it up. Neither bias can be quantified from the snapshot, so the multiple gets a minority weight as a market-based check rather than serving as a primary method. Both legs add the same net cash ($68.274B, see net_cash). The weight is unchanged from round 1, where it was set before the resulting target price was seen.
